extra.message: The OAuth callback helper performs server-side requests.post(url=redirect_uri). In the /consent GET (line 486/494) and POST (line 522/531) handlers redirect_uri is taken directly from request.args and is never checked against ALLOWED_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI (unlike /login at line 394). An attacker can call /consent?consent=true&state=x&redirect_uri=http://169.254.169.254/... to force the server to issue arbitrary requests (SSRF) and to POST the victim's id_token to an attacker-controlled URL (token exfiltration).

redirect_uri comes from request.args in the /consent handler without validation and is used verbatim in redirect(redirect_uri + '#error=access_denied', 302). The same unvalidated value drives redirects at lines 548, 551 and 554, and redirect_uri is echoed into the consent form action at templates/consent.html, enabling an open redirect to arbitrary external sites.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: decode_token() calls jwt.decode(...) with options={"verify_signature": False}, so the JWT signature is not validated and any attacker-forged token is accepted by this helper. It is used for authorization decisions (e.g. account_id = decode_token(token)['acct'] at lines 219/282 and 362), which can lead to authentication/authorization bypass if verification is not enforced by the caller.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: Login credentials are sent to the userservice as GET query parameters (params={'username': username, 'password': password}). Passwords placed in a URL are commonly recorded in browser history, proxy/access logs and monitoring systems. The userservice endpoint reads them via request.args at src/accounts/userservice/userservice.py:175-176.

cwe: CWE-598: Use of GET Request Method With Sensitive Query Strings

extra.message: The /login endpoint accepts the username and password as URL query parameters (request.args.get('username') / request.args.get('password')). Credentials in query strings are exposed to logs, proxies and browser history.

cwe: CWE-598: Use of GET Request Method With Sensitive Query Strings

extra.message: Sender ownership is only enforced when fromRoute.equals(localRoutingNum). Because fromRoutingNum is fully client-controlled, any authenticated user can submit a transaction with a non-local fromRoutingNum and an arbitrary fromAccountNum; the ownership check is skipped and, in LedgerWriterController (line 159) / LedgerMonolithController (line 257), the balance check is also skipped. This lets any authenticated user credit any local account with an arbitrary amount, bypassing authorization and balance controls.

Internal exception details are returned to the client via new ResponseEntity<>(e.getMessage(), HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR). ResourceAccessException/CannotCreateTransactionException/HttpServerErrorException messages can disclose backend hostnames, URLs and database details. The same pattern exists in LedgerMonolithController.java:288-289.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: A complete RSA private key (jwtRS256.key) used to sign authentication JWTs is committed to the repository in cleartext (base64) as a Kubernetes Secret. Anyone with repository access can forge valid tokens for any user. The README itself states the secret should never be checked into version control.
